newsitem.title: USA: Cool, wet weather forecast for U.S. Midwest - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Cool, wet weather forecast for U.S. Midwest - WSC.

text.p: Mostly cool, wet weather was forecast for the U.S. Midwest through next week, and weather maps suggested ample showers next week, said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
"It looks wetter than normal," he said of next week.

Until then, scattered showers and cool weather were forecast for the Midwest, with the near-freezing conditions likely across northern Illinois, northern Indiana and northern Ohio late Friday and early Saturday.
"It looks like it's a fairly cool air mass, but not cold enough to cause any significant (crop) problems," Burgio said.
Rain amounts of 0.2 to 0.6 inch were forecast Wednesday for the western Midwest and 0.25 to 1.00 inch Thursday in eastern areas, said Burgio.
Low temperatures in the mid-30s degrees Fahrenheit were likely late Tuesday and early Wednesday this week in Michigan and northern Ohio, but the coldest system should arrive Friday.
Burgio said lows overnight Friday to early Saturday this week should range from the low 30s across the northern Midwest to high 30s and lows 40s along the southern portion.

Next week also should be cool and wet. The National Weather Service's six-to-10-day outlook predicted much below normal temperatures for Iowa, Illinois and Indiana next week, and above normal precipitation in all but Iowa, which was expected to have normal rainfall.
Scattered showers should fall in the hard red winter wheat areas from Kansas to the Texas Panhandle this week, with greater amounts likely next week, said Burgio.
Thursday and Friday should be cool in the Plains, with warmer weather likely Saturday and Sunday, but Burgio said he doubted the wheat crop faces any serious weather threats through next week.
